summary: Independent review of the log-selection fix for v2_restart_evidence.py. This closes the blocker I reported after restarting oms and reconciler: adding reconciler to --restarted made the tool zcat /var/log/project-mai-tai/reconciler.log-20260731.gz, a six-week-old rotated file that opens at line 1 with a raw Redis asyncio traceback and no preceding timestamp, so the scoping rule raised EvidenceUnknown and voided the entire report with exit 2. The fix threads an optional since= into _log_files and skips any file whose mtime predates the process start, using the mtime the function already collected via find -printf '%T@|%p' and previously discarded. It is the fix I proposed, and it corrects the SELECTION of files rather than weakening the fail-closed rule, which is what I wanted: every file that could contain post-start evidence is still scanned and an unscopeable traceback inside one still voids the report. The boundary is the safe direction: the guard is 'modified_at < cutoff', so a file whose mtime equals the restart instant is KEPT rather than dropped, and test_log_reader_keeps_an_ambiguous_file_at_the_restart_boundary pins that. I also checked the rotation pattern this box actually uses, where logs roll at 00:00 UTC: for a 2026-09-12 20:34 UTC v2 start read on Monday, the file holding 20:34 to midnight has an mtime of 2026-09-13 00:00 and is therefore retained, so the filter cannot drop the boundary file in practice. Mutation matrix, 6 mutations against a baseline of 36 green in the covering file: loosening the boundary to <= turned 2 tests RED, which is the mutation that would have silently dropped a file that matters; removing the filter entirely RED 2, restoring the original July-log bug; inverting the comparison to > RED 2; unscoping the per-service traceback scan from the service start RED 15; and unscoping the v2 warmup and boot-hold scan RED 15. Controlled pair, full unit suite, sorted failure-NAME sets: base 5dae7c9a 46 failed / 3772 passed, head e925ec7d 46 failed / 3775 passed, identical 46 names, zero new failures, and the +3 delta is exactly the three new tests, so the numbers reconcile without residue. Both worktrees were asserted to import their own project_mai_tai before any count was trusted. Base is an ancestor of head; the diff is confined to the tool and its test file. FINDING, recorded rather than blocked, and NOT a regression introduced here. The Tracebacks row renders 'PASS' if traceback_total == 0 with no condition on the denominator, so zero tracebacks out of ZERO scanned timestamped records reads as PASS. I tested whether that is deliberate by adding 'and timestamped_total > 0' to the condition: all 36 tests stayed green, so nothing pins the behaviour and it is unexamined rather than intended. The PASS-on-zero semantics predate this PR, but this PR substantially widens the path to it, because the filter can now legitimately return an empty file list where previously a service always had at least its rotated files scanned. The live example is concrete: the reconciler's log has been 0 bytes since 2026-08-28, so its row will read reconciler=0/0 and contribute PASS every Monday regardless of health, which means that for that service the check cannot come out false. codex-2's statement that the reconciler 'correctly reports 0/0' is accurate as a reading, but a 0/0 service is one we measured nothing about rather than one verified clean. The fix already exists in this tool's own vocabulary: bar continuity reports N/A_OFF_SESSION instead of PASS when it measured nothing, and a restarted service with zero timestamped records wants the same treatment. Requested as a follow-up. Operational note for the merge sequence: the Monday gate pins EXPECTED_SHA=5dae7c9a, so syncing the checkout to the merged SHA requires updating EXPECTED_SHA in preopen.sh in the same action, otherwise the gate fails on checkout identity. CI: validate to be confirmed before I call this pinned.
